page: Amazon Web Services m5a.large is an entry-level general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing two dedicated vCPUs mapped to a single physical core across two hardware threads. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets including AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, but lacking AVX-512 extensions.

The instance comes equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The m5a.large includes no local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent and transient disk needs. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark assessments place the compute and memory throughput in the lower percentiles compared to modern instances. The AMD EPYC 7571 processor achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 722.0 and a multi-core score of 956.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1869.51 and 1611.67 in cryptographic testing. Large-block memory bandwidth registers at 22.95 GB/sec for reads and 13.58 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, the server managed 1.22 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.55 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Because of its legacy CPU architecture and modest two-thread capacity, the m5a.large represents an economical general-purpose entry point where computational speed is secondary to basic memory and architectural stability. The instance is suited for lightweight workloads such as development environments, small-scale web servers, background task workers, low-traffic APIs, and auxiliary microservices that do not require high computational density or dedicated GPU acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.large is a general-purpose virtual instance configured on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads. It features 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring external network-attached volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps without hardware accelerators. Synthetic benchmarks reflect entry-tier processing capacity, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 956.0 and Redis throughput of 1.22 million operations per second. The instance provides an economical allocation of memory and dedicated vCPUs for low-intensity applications, including staging environments, light web servers, basic automation workers, and small auxiliary microservices.
